comparisons.evidence: P's "Commit–Reveal Book" makes prior interpretation "temporarily irreversible," and "Succession Palimpsest" makes reading alter future readability; Q's "Rule-Later Edition" and "Model-Boundary Edition" mainly improve model formation within familiar reading workflows. P's strongest mechanisms would more fundamentally expand what reading can be.

P's "Pulse-Gated Prose" assumes physiological transitions indicate cognitive readiness, while "Succession Palimpsest" assumes irreversible alteration improves interpretation. Q gives tighter pathways, such as cases producing a provisional rule before correction in "Rule-Later" and independent encodings making misunderstanding detectable in "Error-Correcting Edition."

P's "Future-Self Secret Share" requires delayed installments and memory-dependent reconstruction, and "Succession Palimpsest" requires destructible physical production. Q's "Rule-Later" can be tested by rewriting twelve pages, while "Context-Locked" uses a simple envelope booklet, creating lower adoption and production barriers.

P concretely specifies that readers record expectations and falsifiers before evidence, then proposes a controlled six-page test. Q specifies a four-part "Rule-Later" unit and an unfamiliar transfer problem. Both make the user operation and cheapest prototype readily understandable.

P introduces unusual but coherent levers such as a book whose layers are physically transformed by reading and complementary fragments distributed across a reader's "past, present, and future" selves. Q's "Rule-Later" and "Model-Boundary" are useful reframings, but remain closer to established instructional sequencing and conceptual chunking.

P spans belief precommitment, physiological gating, destructive material transformation, grammatical decomposition, spatial folding, temporal self-separation, and meaning through textual mutation. Q spans contextual timing, hypothesis generation, redundancy, evidence ordering, and longitudinal annotation, but more of its portfolio clusters around correcting or externalizing mental models.

P ultimately promotes the high-friction "Future-Self Secret Share" despite explicitly anticipating "unacceptable dropout," alongside the production-heavy "Succession Palimpsest." Q removes mechanisms likely to become "interpretive busywork" and recommends a more consistently useful set: "Rule-Later," "Model-Boundary," "Context-Locked," and "Error-Correcting."
